evidence: Hor. S. 1.5.96: postera tempestās melior, via pejor
terms.comment: The ordinary word for any road, in town or country; the great highways are viae with names (via Appia).

terms.gloss: the way one takes, a route; a journey
evidence: Cic. Att. 4.3.4: iter dēvium, a side road (Lewis & Short s.v. dēvius)
M-O s.v. road: backroad, secondary road
terms.comment: The going, or the route taken, more than the road itself.

terms.gloss: a street lined with houses, in a town; a village

terms.comment: Short for via strāta, a paved road; the source of English street.

phrases.english: the next day the weather was better, the road worse

phrases.latin: tantum lutī tōtā viā fuit ut possim vidērī nihilōminus nāvigāsse
phrases.english: there was so much mud the whole way that I might as well have gone by sea

phrases.latin: omnis enim fermē via praeceps, angusta, lūbrica erat
phrases.english: for almost the whole road was steep, narrow and slippery
